feature.name: Birdie call identification
feature.viewer: home birders who hear birds outside their window
feature.task: catch a bird's call with a tiny mic and get its name, then keep it in a logbook
feature.before: you hear birds singing outside but can't tell which ones
feature.after: every call is named, logged and replayable

beats.picture: a hand holds the tiny I2S mic, the camera travels left to the breadboard rig by the window, and a teal listening dot lights on the mic
beats.carrier: the teal listening dot flies off the mic into the phone's Listening pill

beats.picture: the phone listens, the bird card resolves and flips to the Indian Roller; then 100+ species resolves through a pixel front, dissolves outside-in, and eight logbook birds swirl clockwise around the Birdie badge
beats.take: a big amber number resolves left to right through a pixel front inside a hairline panel, holds, dissolves from both ends while the panel narrows to a square, then upright tiles swirl in clockwise on a collapsing radius and keep orbiting a centre badge until they exit clockwise
ui: the app is listening: the sketched card shimmers as the call is matched
the match lands: the card turns into the Indian Roller photo with its name
beats.carrier: the Birdie mark from the badge centre travels up-left into the corner

beats.picture: the Radar list of birds heard today scrolls, the day's call chart fills, then the Logbook grid of collected birds
ui: tap Radar: the list of species heard today with call counts
tap Logbook: the grid of collected birds with their call counts
beats.carrier: the Birdie mark travels from the corner into the end card

beats.picture: the Birdie mark lands over a window of moving aurora light
